headline: Liquor Board Fines Haʻikū Market $2,000 for Minor Decoy Sale

meeting.body: Liquor Board Fines Haʻikū Market $2,000 for Minor Decoy Sale
meeting.summary: The board fined the owner of Haʻikū Market $1,000 on each of two counts after a cashier sold alcohol to an 18-year-old decoy.
meeting.recap: The board took up complaint and accusation 2026-15 against the owner of Haʻikū Market.[[0:00:00]] The store's attorney said the business pleaded no contest to counts one and two.[[0:00:38]] Under the plea deal, the department agreed to drop count three.[[0:01:14]] The board accepted the plea and found the business guilty of counts one and two.[[0:02:23]] The department said an 18-year-old decoy bought a 5% alcohol drink at the store on July 8th, 2025.[[0:03:17]] The cashier asked for her ID, looked at it, and sold her the drink.[[0:03:58]] Count one is selling liquor to a minor, and count two is failing to check ID properly.[[0:04:28]] He said each register asks for a birth date, but the cashier did not enter it properly.[[0:06:07]] The department recommended $2,000 per count, with $1,000 of each suspended for one year if there are no more violations.[[0:10:02]] The store asked the board to consider its clean record.[[0:10:40]] The board voted to go into closed session (a private discussion) to decide the penalty.[[0:10:58]] Back in open session, the board voted unanimously to fine the business $1,000 on each count.[[0:12:02]]
decided: The board accepted the no contest plea and found the business guilty of counts one and two, with count three dismissed by agreement.
The board voted by roll call to go into closed session to deliberate.
The board voted unanimously to fine the business $1,000 on count one and $1,000 on count two.
meeting.next: The business will be notified when payment of the fine is due.
